text:
sara: Quick follow-up from the RFC — we need to decide how much of the precision profile we actually expose in the public inference API. Do we: (A) expose named profiles (high/medium/low) that map to internal per-layer settings, or (B) let clients specify a per-layer/parameter precision object?
ben: my vote is A. surface simplicity wins for customers + avoids accidental bad configs.
tim: A seems safer, but we should make the named profiles composable/extendable so power users can opt-in.
sara: Agreed. Problem with A is ops visibility: we still need enough metadata to route to the right runtime variant and for telemetry (expected quality delta).
anya: can we encode a small capability token in the request that says which profile-level guarantees they want (eg: "min_quality": "0.95", "cost_tier": "low")? then runtime picks best profile that meets constraint. :thinking:
ben: that sounds like a good contract. keeps user-facing API simple while letting runtime pick internal mapping. also helps routing across dedicated vs hosted.
sara: sketch of a minimal request snippet I ran locally — happy to iterate:
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "redwood-3b",
  "precision_profile": "balanced",
  "quality_goal": 0.98,
  "max_cost_multiplier": 1.2,
  "prompt": "..."
}
```
ben: two concerns: 1) how do we validate quality_goal across model families? 2) is precision_profile versioned? if we change what "balanced" means later we need strong semantic versioning.
tim: for (1) we need a per-model calibration layer. a small manifest that maps named-profile -> expected regression windows / confidence intervals. for (2) include a profile_version token and default to the latest stable if not provided.
anya: ops question — what happens if runtime can't meet quality_goal at requested cost? fall back or return 4xx? we should avoid surprising production apps.
sara: proposal: runtime returns a header X-Precision-Fallback: <policy> and a transparent body field fallback_applied: true plus reason. default policy is "best-effort-with-notify"; customers can opt into strict-mode which returns error.
ben: telemetry-wise we need to emit both chosen internal precision plan and the predicted vs observed quality delta so we can train the mapping. Instrumentation point: per-request chosen_profile_id, predicted_score, observed_score.
tim: also add a short-circuit safety net: if observed_score drops below acceptable threshold, route to a higher-fidelity model variant immediately. that's our graceful degradation.
sara: ops-bot note: can we add an automated canary gate? e.g., new profile_version only rolled to 1% traffic, and we block rollout if degradation rate > 0.5% over 24h.
ops-bot: Deploy plan registered: profile_version "balanced-v2" -> canary 1%. Alert rule: quality_regression_rate > 0.5% in 24h -> rollback.
anya: curious about on-prem/private customers — they might want to bake their own mapping. allow profile override via admin config?
ben: yes, allow customer-managed profile manifests in Private deployments. default to our verified ones for Hosted/Dedicated.
sara: last thought on UX: docs should show typical tradeoffs with short examples (tokens/sec, cost delta, example prompts where lowbit fails). keep it developer-friendly.
tim: I'll draft the manifest schema and the calibration interface this week and post an RFC follow-up with examples and telemetry fields.
sara: thanks — let's capture these action items: 1) manifest schema + profile_versioning (tim) 2) request fields + fallback headers (sara) 3) telemetry contract (ben) 4) canary rollout guards (ops) 5) docs examples (anya).
ben: noted. :thumbsup:
anya: thanks everyone, feels much clearer.
sara: cool — closing the thread, will loop the product folks after RFC update.
